plain_english_policy: This bill allows the School Superintendents of Alabama to independently enroll their executive officers and employees in the Teachers' Retirement System (TRS) without needing an affiliation agreement with the Council for Leaders in Alabama Schools. If they choose this option, the governing body must pass a resolution authorizing it. The school superintendents would then pay the employer's share of contributions based on employee salaries, paid monthly alongside employee deductions. Benefits received by these employees and their beneficiaries are limited to what was contributed plus interest earned minus administrative costs; no additional state funding is required beyond the standard contribution rules.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would authorize a structural change in how executive staff of school superintendents participate in retirement, shifting from reliance on an external council affiliation to direct participation managed by the School Superintendents themselves. This expands administrative flexibility for local education leadership while maintaining strict financial limits where benefits cannot exceed contributions plus interest.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Lindsey (Education Appropriations) supports expanding retirement participation options for school superintendents' staff.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would authorize the executive officers and employees of the School Superintendents of Alabama to independently continue to participate in the Teachers' Retirement System."

"The governing body of the School Superintendents of Alabama... may elect to have its executive officers and employees... continue eligibility to participate in the Teachers' Retirement System of Alabama, subject to all rules, regulations, and conditions thereof."
